content.purpose: Inspect a directory before choosing a file or changing anything.
content.mentalModel: ls reads directory entries. Options change which entries are shown and how their metadata is presented; they do not change the files.

demonstration.explanation: This small example isolates the main idea behind listing files with ls.

remember: ls reads directory entries. Options change which entries are shown and how their metadata is presented; they do not change the files.

tasks.instruction: List every entry in /home/student/lab/catalog except . and .., sort the names, and save them to /home/student/answers/catalog-list.txt.
hints: The ordinary listing hides names beginning with a dot.
Use ls -A to include hidden entries without adding . and ...
Pipe the listing through sort before redirecting it.
